doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

chapter: Early life and path into trad jazz
title: Starting on cornet and learning to improvise in a restaurant band
summary: Dave played cornet and piano, then led a trad band for peanuts at a local restaurant for six years, which taught him to improvise. He is a weekend warrior.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well I didn’t start out with the intention of doing either one. I enjoyed playing cornet in high school and college, trumpet and cornet, and took piano lessons for a while. And actually at some point when I was young I thought I’d probably continue with piano and drop the horn but somehow it worked out the other way around. I could never get the two hands coordinated. And so I stayed with the horn through college and then wasn’t sure if I would continue but I had by then a very strong interest in jazz, specifically traditional jazz. So when I got out of college a guy helped me put a band together to play traditional jazz for almost literally peanuts in a local restaurant. It was beer and snacks and a couple of bucks. But I did that for six years and that was my apprenticeship. That’s how I learned to improvise, just by doing that every week.

So I wound up being a horn player and from there I went on to — I’m not a full time player, I’m what they call a weekend warrior, I play evenings and weekends. But I do a lot of gigging and have done a little bit or touring and have been very glad that I’ve stayed with that.
